content: {"summary":"Current safeguards include a lock_timeout set on Alembic migrations (added after May 2025) that limits how long a migration can wait for a lock, connection‑pool caps that restrict catalog‑api to at most 30 DB sessions, and active monitoring of catalog‑db CPU and lock‑related metrics to trigger alerts.","likely_cause":"lock_timeout on migrations prevents indefinite lock waits","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A lock_timeout was added after May 2025 so migrations no longer wait indefinitely for locks","evidence_ids":["RB-028#1"],"quote":"There was no `lock_timeout` on migrations then. It dates from 2025-05-16, the day after."},{"text":"Each catalog‑api pod’s SQLAlchemy pool allows 10 connections plus 5 overflow, capping sessions at 30","evidence_ids":["RB-028#1"],"quote":"Each pod's SQLAlchemy pool allows 10 connections plus 5 overflow, so at most 30 sessions"},{"text":"Operators watch catalog‑db CPU and lock‑rate metrics to detect contention early","evidence_ids":["RB-017#3"],"quote":"Watch catalog-db-01.prod.internal CPU and the `CAT-E301` rate side by side"}],"next_checks":["Confirm the current lock_timeout value and that it is applied to all migration jobs","Verify that the connection‑pool settings are still enforced in production pods","Ensure monitoring alerts for catalog‑db CPU and CAT‑E301 rate are active and have appropriate thresholds"]}
